blocks.content: Regional Rural Banks were established with a view to developing the rural economy by providing credit and other facilities for agriculture and other productive activities in rural areas.

The Priority Sector Lending (PSL) target for RRBs is 75%, which is significantly higher than the 40% required for Scheduled Commercial Banks.
RRBs were legally formalized under the Regional Rural Banks Act of 1976.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established on October 2, 1975, based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group.
Prathama Bank in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh, sponsored by Syndicate Bank, was the first Regional Rural Bank set up in India.
The equity structure of every RRB is shared between the Central Government (50%), State Government (15%), and the Sponsor Bank (35%).
RRBs operate under the regulatory oversight of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and are supervised by NABARD.
RRBs are required to extend 75% of their total Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to Priority Sector Lending.
